verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents an open-source self-host path: Docker Compose bundles MongoDB, the API and the front-end, and a self-hostable proxy can serve flags locally. A hands-on probe booted the official Docker image and completed a full create-and-evaluate flag loop with no account or license. Evaluation stays on your infrastructure: the SDKs evaluate locally and attribute values are never sent to GrowthBook, and community users confirm running it self-hosted on their own data. Missing for 10: confirmation that pricing-gated features (SSO/SCIM, approval workflows, audit logs) are included in the open-source self-hosted distribution, and a documented non-Docker install path.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Open Source Feature Flags, Experimentation, and Product Analytics
a real flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license.
The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook. They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.
One company has used the self-hosted version for a few months and is very happy with it; issues get resolved quickly.
